provenance.encoder: Morgan FP + metal descriptor block + cell one-hot (build_design)

arms.zero_shot: train on the other four metals, no adaptation
arms.offset: zero-shot + mean residual shift from k points (EXT-3 baseline)
arms.ridge: zero-shot + closed-form ridge on k residuals in the design space
arms.proto: zero-shot + cosine-softmax weighted residual average over k prototypes

design.sampling: whole DOI groups (sample_calibration), calibration rows excluded from scoring

verdict_rule: PASS iff at k=50 the best arm has >= 3/5 metals with mean R2 >= 0
caveats: The encoder is a fixed Morgan-FP design matrix, not a meta-trained D-MPNN. The D-MPNN checkpoints were deleted on 2026-10-21; re-encoding is a separate run.
ridge and proto adapt a residual, so they cannot fix a systematically wrong ranking; they only move the level. That is the same limitation as offset, partially lifted.
Calibration rows are drawn per repeat with whole-DOI grouping, so different repeats see different amounts of data for the same k.

proto collapsed onto offset (see diagnostics): in a 2048-bit Morgan space the cosine similarities are near-constant, so the softmax weights are uniform. The ProtoNet arm was therefore not independently tested.

diagnostics.reading: True means the cosine similarities in the Morgan design space are near-constant, the softmax over the k prototypes is uniform, and the proto arm is the plain mean. It is NOT an independent adaptation family in this encoder.
